nodes.label: Fund Accounting & NAV
nodes.description: The Accounting Book of Record: double-entry books per fund, accruals, fees and the shadow NAV that is reconciled to the administrator’s official NAV.
nodes.run_model: Business hours; month-end and filing peaks

nodes.label: Fund Administrator
nodes.description: An independent third party that calculates the official NAV, keeps the books of record for investors and auditors, and often acts as transfer agent.

nodes.label: Alternative Data Providers
nodes.description: Non-traditional datasets used for signals: card transaction panels, satellite imagery, web traffic, app downloads, shipping, sentiment.

nodes.label: API & Integration
nodes.description: One controlled way in and out for APIs and files: internal service APIs, partner APIs, and the SFTP estate that still carries most counterparty data.

nodes.label: Audit & Records
nodes.description: Books-and-records retention, communications archiving and a tamper-evident audit trail that regulators and auditors can rely on.

nodes.label: Event Backbone
nodes.description: A durable integration backbone for versioned business events. Systems of record remain authoritative for their domains; downstream consumers build projections, reconcile them, and can replay retained events where the contract supports it.
nodes.run_model: 24×7 for the backbone; business hours for analytics

nodes.label: Capital Allocation
nodes.description: The CIO’s engine for allocating capital dynamically across strategy groups and investment teams, based on opportunity, risk-adjusted performance and correlation to the rest of the book. It owns each team’s capital, drawdown rules and payout calculation, and gives senior management one live view of the firm.

nodes.label: Margin & Collateral
nodes.description: Manages margin with prime brokers, clearing brokers and OTC counterparties, and optimises the use of collateral and financing.

nodes.label: Compliance Engine
nodes.description: Encodes regulatory, mandate and internal rules. It checks every order before it trades and every portfolio afterwards, and keeps the evidence.

nodes.label: Matching & Affirmation
nodes.description: Central utilities that match the fund’s allocations with the broker’s confirmations so trades can settle on time. Essential for US T+1.

nodes.label: Custodians & CSDs
nodes.description: Banks and central securities depositories that hold assets not held at the prime broker and settle trades.

nodes.label: Execution Management
nodes.description: The trader’s tool for working orders. It chooses brokers, algos and venues, slices orders, and measures execution quality.

nodes.label: FIX & Connectivity
nodes.description: Manages every electronic session to brokers, venues and RFQ platforms, normalises messages, and isolates the internal stack from the outside world.

nodes.label: Identity & Entitlements
nodes.description: Who can see and do what, everywhere: single sign-on, role and attribute-based access, information barriers and maker-checker as a shared service.

nodes.label: IBOR · Positions
nodes.description: The Investment Book of Record: the real-time, front-office view of positions and cash, built from trades, allocations and corporate actions.
nodes.run_model: Follow-the-sun L2 aligned to operations shifts

nodes.label: Infrastructure & DR
nodes.description: Runtime for everything: public cloud for elastic workloads, colocation near exchanges where latency matters, with tested disaster recovery.

nodes.label: Investor Portal
nodes.description: Self-service access to investor documents and account information. Verition’s website links to Northern Trust’s investor portal. Confirm separately the administration, TA, dealing and fund-accounting services and their data interfaces.

nodes.label: Investors / LPs
nodes.description: Pension funds, endowments, sovereign wealth funds, funds of funds, family offices and high-net-worth individuals.

nodes.label: Lakehouse & Analytics
nodes.description: The governed analytical history for events, positions, prices and risk results. It serves research, finance, regulatory reporting and analytics without sitting on the live order path.

nodes.label: Market Data Vendors
nodes.description: Real-time quotes and trades, end-of-day closes, curves, volatility surfaces and evaluated prices for OTC and fixed income.

nodes.label: Pricing & Market Data
nodes.description: Normalises real-time and end-of-day market data, builds curves and volatility surfaces, and produces the independent official price set used for NAV.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.description: Technical and business monitoring: latency, errors and saturation, plus business signals such as “no fills from broker X in 10 minutes”.

nodes.label: Order Management
nodes.description: The system of record for orders, from PM intent through compliance, trader working and fills to allocation across funds.

nodes.label: Operations Console
nodes.description: One workspace for operations, fund accounting and treasury: exception queues, settlement status, cash, corporate action elections and NAV sign-off.

nodes.label: OTC Dealers & RFQ
nodes.description: Dealers and electronic RFQ platforms for bonds, swaps, credit and FX, including swap execution facilities.

nodes.label: Prime Brokers
nodes.description: Banks that finance the fund’s positions, lend stock for shorts, hold assets, provide swaps and calculate margin.

nodes.label: Portfolio Management
nodes.description: Each investment team’s view of its book: real-time positions, exposures and P&L, with tools to construct portfolios, model trades and generate orders. Every team gets the same tooling; entitlements decide what each team can see, and sharing across teams is the default unless a wall applies.

nodes.label: PM & Trader Workstation
nodes.description: The desktop where portfolio managers and traders see the book, model trades, and send and work orders. It is a client of the PMS, OMS, EMS and risk engine and holds no state of its own.
nodes.run_model: Follow-the-sun L2 with trading support desk L1

nodes.label: Trade Support
nodes.description: Turns executed blocks into confirmed, affirmed allocations ready to settle, and keeps brokers and prime brokers in sync.

nodes.label: Reconciliation
nodes.description: Compares internal books with prime brokers, custodians, brokers and the administrator, and drives every break to resolution.

nodes.label: Reference Data Vendors
nodes.description: Instrument terms, identifiers, issuer hierarchies and corporate action announcements.

nodes.label: Regulators
nodes.description: Authorities that receive filings, examine the firm and set the rules encoded in compliance and reporting.

nodes.label: Regulatory & Investor Reporting
nodes.description: Produces regulatory filings and investor reports from governed data in accounting, risk and the lakehouse.

nodes.label: Research & Signals
nodes.description: Where investment ideas and quantitative signals are generated, tested and promoted into the portfolio process. For most funds this is the edge, so it is built.

nodes.label: Risk Engine
nodes.description: Independent measurement of market, liquidity and counterparty risk, in tiers: each investment team watches its own risk intraday, central risk nets exposures across teams and sets limits, and an external provider independently checks the numbers. Feeds capital allocation, compliance and regulatory reporting.
nodes.run_model: Market-hours L2; independent model validation in risk

nodes.label: Security Master
nodes.description: The golden source of instrument identity, terms, issuers and corporate actions. Every other system refers to securities by its internal ID.

nodes.label: Settlement & Treasury
nodes.description: Instructs and tracks settlement of securities and cash, manages payments, funding and FX, and forecasts liquidity.

nodes.label: Investor Services
nodes.description: Manages investors’ interests in the funds: onboarding, KYC, subscriptions, redemptions, transfers and capital account statements. Often delivered by the administrator.

nodes.label: Exchanges & MTFs
nodes.description: Lit exchanges, multilateral trading facilities, dark pools and futures exchanges reached by direct market access or through brokers.

nodes.label: CDC connectors
nodes.description: Turn vendor databases into event streams.

nodes.label: Performance analytics
nodes.description: How every team is really doing.

nodes.label: Drawdown & stop rules
nodes.description: Protects the firm from any single team.

nodes.label: Senior management cockpit
nodes.description: One live picture of the firm.

nodes.label: Margin calculator
nodes.description: What we owe and are owed.

nodes.label: Capital markets & wall-crossing
nodes.description: Participation in new issues without MNPI leaks.

nodes.label: Algo & broker selection
nodes.description: Who works the order and how.

nodes.label: Rules-based router
nodes.description: Sends each message to the right session.

nodes.label: Session monitoring
nodes.description: Knows when a link is unhealthy.

nodes.label: Position calculator
nodes.description: Positions as a fold over events.

nodes.label: Start-of-day roll
nodes.description: Opens each day from a reconciled base.

nodes.label: Cash projection
nodes.description: Expected cash by currency and date.

nodes.label: Corporate action processor
nodes.description: Applies CAs to positions and lots.

nodes.label: Ingestion & CDC
nodes.description: Streams backbone topics into raw tables.

nodes.label: Bitemporal model
nodes.description: Stores what was true and when we knew it.

nodes.label: Feature store
nodes.description: Shared signal inputs with consistent definitions.

nodes.label: Query & BI
nodes.description: SQL, notebooks and dashboards for analysts.

nodes.label: Feed handlers
nodes.description: Connect to vendor and exchange feeds.

nodes.label: EOD pricing engine
nodes.description: The official price set for books and NAV.

nodes.label: Compliance gateway
nodes.description: No order to market without a pass.

nodes.label: New-issue orders
nodes.description: IPOs, follow-ons, convertibles and bond deals.

nodes.label: Exception inbox
nodes.description: Common queue for breaks from every ops system.

nodes.label: Settlement dashboard
nodes.description: Status of today’s and failing settlements.

nodes.label: NAV checklist
nodes.description: Daily and monthly close tasks with evidence.

nodes.label: Optimiser & construction
nodes.description: Turns views into a target portfolio.

nodes.label: Grid & blotter framework
nodes.description: High-frequency data grids for positions, orders and fills.

nodes.label: Order ticket
nodes.description: Single, basket and program order entry with validation.

nodes.label: Real-time gateway
nodes.description: Pushes position, price and order updates to the browser.

nodes.label: Desktop interop
nodes.description: Window management and context sharing between apps.

nodes.label: Reporting data mart
nodes.description: One governed source for every report.

nodes.label: Backtesting engine
nodes.description: Simulates a strategy as it would have traded.

nodes.label: Factor model
nodes.description: Explains risk and P&L by factor.

nodes.label: Liquidity risk
nodes.description: Can we exit and meet redemptions.

nodes.label: Firm-level netting & crowding
nodes.description: What the firm holds, not what each team holds.

nodes.label: Vendor adapters
nodes.description: Parse and normalise each vendor feed.

nodes.label: Entity & issuer master
nodes.description: Who issued what and who owns whom.

nodes.label: Instrument setup workflow
nodes.description: On-demand creation for new OTC and private instruments.

nodes.label: Source capital & mandates
nodes.measure: Subscriptions and redemptions processed correctly by dealing date

nodes.label: Gate 3 · Institutionalise
nodes.title: Finance, investor & regulatory outcomes
tasks: Reconcile IBOR to accounting and administrator outputs; establish NAV sign-off
Deliver governed investor and regulatory reporting for confirmed entities
Formalise fee, expense, allocation and payout rules against contracts
Add evidence, retention, access certification, surveillance and DR exercises

nodes.label: Onboard & run teams
nodes.measure: Elapsed time from approved team to first controlled trade

nodes.label: Gate 2 · Broaden
nodes.title: Shared control plane
tasks: Extend team, fund, instrument and capital hierarchies
Add central risk, independent challenge and limit / drawdown workflows
Bring in more PB, broker, venue and asset-class connections
Add cash, collateral, corporate actions, settlement and exception ownership
Scale research sharing with MNPI, licensing and team-confidentiality controls

nodes.label: Gate 1 · Prove
nodes.title: One controlled vertical slice
tasks: Select one representative workflow and asset class with business owners
Integrate approved reference data, PM / OMS, risk and execution systems
Prove order checks, fills, booking, reconciliation and audit end to end
Add a versioned research dataset and a reproducible discretionary or quant use case
Set operational SLOs from measured workflows and test failure / replay

nodes.label: Size & risk-check
nodes.measure: Orders with complete intent and pre-trade result

nodes.label: Account, NAV & report
nodes.measure: Price and corporate-action coverage by cut-off

nodes.label: Review & reallocate capital
nodes.measure: Capital decisions with scope, effective time and downstream acknowledgement

nodes.label: Gate 4 · Optimise
nodes.title: Measure and extend the edge
tasks: Use TCA and realised outcomes in research and execution review
Expand systematic signal promotion and model monitoring where needed
Automate high-volume workflows only after exception rates are stable
Tune cost, performance and regional topology from observed use
Retire duplicate tools only after reconciliation and owner sign-off

nodes.label: Gate 0 · Discover
nodes.title: Current-state & control baseline
tasks: Inventory systems, contracts, owners, interfaces and data rights
Map one end-to-end research and trade workflow per strategy group
Confirm funds, legal entities, jurisdictions, control owners and record schedules
Measure volumes, cut-offs, latency, availability and recovery needs
Decide retain / integrate / replace by capability; validate risk platform and administrator scope

nodes.label: Browser or desktop container?
nodes.context: Traders run many windows across several monitors next to Bloomberg and broker apps.
nodes.revisit: Traders ask for linked windows across apps, or you adopt FDC3 with vendors.

nodes.label: Which grid technology?
nodes.context: Blotters stream thousands of updates per second and need grouping, pivoting and export.
nodes.revisit: Licence cost becomes material or a team needs pivots over very large data.

nodes.label: How is real-time data delivered?
nodes.context: Prices tick far faster than humans can read; positions update on every fill.
nodes.revisit: Never for trading; GraphQL is fine for ops and reporting screens.

nodes.label: Own the UI or use vendor screens?
nodes.context: Vendor OMS and PMS products ship their own front ends.
nodes.revisit: PMs spend most of their day switching between vendor screens.

nodes.label: Which workflow engine?
nodes.context: NAV close, CA elections and approvals are long-running, multi-step processes with deadlines.
nodes.revisit: Operations leads want to edit process flows without engineers.

nodes.label: One exception inbox or vendor screens?
nodes.context: Breaks live in the recon tool, fails in the settlement system, mismatches in CTM.
nodes.revisit: You consolidate onto one operations platform.

nodes.label: Low-code or custom for internal tools?
nodes.context: There is a long tail of small screens: SSI approvals, fee rebates, static data requests.
nodes.revisit: A low-code app becomes critical or high-volume; rebuild it.

nodes.label: Who provides the portal?
nodes.context: Investors expect statements, documents and dealing online.
nodes.revisit: Investor relations needs a richer experience or a separate service is contractually required.

nodes.label: How are documents delivered?
nodes.context: Statements and K-1s contain sensitive data.
nodes.revisit: Never fully; allow exceptions by investor with approval.

nodes.label: Which lakehouse platform?
nodes.context: Data vendors increasingly deliver through cloud shares; quants want notebooks and Spark.
nodes.revisit: Compute spend passes the cost of a platform team.

nodes.label: Where does tick data live?
nodes.context: Intraday research needs as-of joins over years of quotes and trades.
nodes.revisit: A quant team’s research is bottlenecked on tick queries.

nodes.label: How is history kept?
nodes.context: You must reproduce any past NAV and any backtest exactly.
nodes.revisit: Never for books and records.

nodes.label: Which orchestrator?
nodes.context: Hundreds of dependent jobs with SLAs.
nodes.revisit: You already run Airflow at scale.

nodes.label: Where is Data Vault used?
nodes.context: Multi-source masters need history of what each source said; high-volume facts and events do not.
nodes.selected: Data Vault for multi-source masters only
nodes.revisit: The team cannot sustain the skills, or mappings stay simple enough for dimensional models.
options: Data Vault for multi-source masters only
Data Vault for all conformed data
No Data Vault: bitemporal dimensional models

nodes.label: Data Vault for multi-source masters only
Data Vault for all conformed data
No Data Vault: bitemporal dimensional models
Where is the ontology held and who changes it?
nodes.context: Definitions, relationships and metrics must stay consistent across the vault, marts, semantic layer and AI context.
nodes.selected: Versioned files in git, owned by the data governance council
nodes.revisit: Stewards cannot work in the review process, or a catalogue tool can export reliably.
options: Versioned files in git, owned by the data governance council
Inside a catalogue or governance tool

nodes.label: Versioned files in git, owned by the data governance council
Inside a catalogue or governance tool
Buy an EDM product or build a thin master?
nodes.context: Security masters are where data quality is won or lost.
nodes.revisit: CA errors keep reaching positions, or asset classes multiply.
options: Use the operations platform’s master (Arcesium, Enfusion)

nodes.label: Use the operations platform’s master (Arcesium, Enfusion)
What is the primary identifier?
nodes.context: Every system must agree what a security is.
nodes.revisit: Never change the key; add identifiers as attributes.

nodes.label: Where do corporate actions come from?
nodes.context: A missed CA silently corrupts positions and P&L.
nodes.revisit: CA volume grows enough to justify a specialist CA vendor.
options: Custodian notices as a third source

nodes.label: Custodian notices as a third source
Which real-time source?
nodes.context: Market data is one of the largest non-people costs.
nodes.revisit: Market data cost per team becomes a capital-allocation issue.

nodes.label: How are ticks distributed internally?
nodes.context: Ticks are high-volume and only the latest value matters.
nodes.revisit: Tick volume is low enough that Kafka alone suffices.

nodes.label: Who sets the official EOD price?
nodes.context: Valuation independence is a regulatory and investor due-diligence expectation.
nodes.revisit: Never hand final marks to PMs.

nodes.label: Which streaming platform?
nodes.context: This is the spine; reliability matters more than features.
nodes.revisit: Spend exceeds the cost of running it yourselves with confidence.

nodes.label: How far do you take event sourcing?
nodes.context: Event sourcing gives perfect audit and replay but adds complexity.
nodes.revisit: A domain needs reproducible state at arbitrary points in time and can own event-schema evolution.

nodes.label: Which serialisation format?
nodes.context: Schemas are the platform’s contracts.
nodes.revisit: Most consumers are data-lake tools that prefer Avro.

nodes.label: How granular are topics?
nodes.context: Too few topics mix concerns; too many become unmanageable.
nodes.revisit: A single event type dominates volume.

nodes.label: Where does research compute run?
nodes.context: Research is bursty: idle overnight, then hundreds of cores for a parameter sweep.
nodes.revisit: Platform operations distract from research support.

nodes.label: What kind of backtester?
nodes.context: Fast iteration and realistic fills pull in opposite directions.
nodes.revisit: Strategies are low-turnover enough that vectorised results match.

nodes.label: How much do investment teams share?
nodes.context: Verition’s published philosophy emphasises collaboration across teams. The proposed library supports discovery and attribution while enforcing confidentiality, MNPI and contractual boundaries.
nodes.selected: Shared by default, walled by exception
nodes.revisit: A team’s contract requires its research to stay private.
options: Shared by default, walled by exception

nodes.label: Shared by default, walled by exception
How is cross-team contribution credited?
nodes.context: If one team’s idea drives another team’s P&L, collaboration only lasts if it is recognised.
nodes.selected: Idea attribution in the research library
nodes.revisit: Never fully; keep it lightweight.
options: Idea attribution in the research library

nodes.label: Idea attribution in the research library
Buy, build, or layer?
nodes.context: PMs judge the whole platform by this screen.
nodes.revisit: The vendor’s analytics are good enough for every team.
options: Bundled with the OMS (Enfusion, CRD, AIM)

nodes.label: Bundled with the OMS (Enfusion, CRD, AIM)
Where is P&L calculated?
nodes.context: Different P&L numbers on different screens destroy trust.
nodes.revisit: Never in a multi-manager platform.

nodes.label: Can teams net or cross orders?
nodes.context: Teams often trade opposite sides of the same name.
nodes.revisit: Opposite-side volume across teams becomes a material cost.

nodes.label: What role should Photon play?
nodes.context: Assess the reported licensed platform across Verition’s four strategy groups; detailed capabilities and production status are not established publicly.
nodes.revisit: A formal product and operating review confirms a wider or narrower scope.
options: Keep as a limited research / comparison source

nodes.label: Keep as a limited research / comparison source
How should Photon receive data?
nodes.context: A proposed Photon integration needs approved, supportable interfaces while preserving clear ownership of positions and accounting books.
nodes.revisit: The product is formally selected as the IBOR and the other book is retired.
options: Point integrations to OMS and PBs

nodes.label: Point integrations to OMS and PBs
What rights and continuity are needed for Photon?
nodes.context: Confirm the actual licence, support, data portability, source-access and exit terms before production dependency grows.
nodes.revisit: Contract review and product diligence establish the actual dependency profile.

nodes.label: Which factor model?
nodes.context: Central risk may use common factor exposures to compare teams and identify concentration; validate the desired model universe and reporting requirements.
nodes.revisit: Investors require a specific vendor in reporting.

nodes.label: Which VaR method?
nodes.context: Each method fails in different ways.
nodes.revisit: Options exposure becomes a large share of firm risk.

nodes.label: Real-time or EOD limits?
nodes.context: In multi-manager funds the drawdown stop is the most important control.
nodes.selected: Intraday for gross, net, drawdown and concentration
nodes.revisit: Never relax for drawdown.
options: Intraday for gross, net, drawdown and concentration

nodes.label: Intraday for gross, net, drawdown and concentration
How are risk numbers independently checked?
nodes.context: Verition publicly describes internal and external risk controls. Proposed independent checks should challenge the inputs, models and outputs of Photon and other engines.
nodes.revisit: Investors or the board ask for daily independent risk.

nodes.label: Where is risk computed?
nodes.context: Risk needs elastic compute at EOD and fast queries during the day.
nodes.revisit: The risk team is too small to own a grid.

nodes.label: Which rules engine?
nodes.context: Every order must be checked in milliseconds, with no path around it.
nodes.revisit: Teams run on several OMSs.

nodes.label: How are custom rules written?
nodes.context: Rules change with regulation and team mandates.
nodes.selected: Rules as code with a test harness
nodes.revisit: Compliance wants to self-serve simple threshold changes.
options: Rules as code with a test harness

nodes.label: Rules as code with a test harness
Firm-wide or team-level restrictions after a wall-crossing?
nodes.context: A deal team may be wall-crossed while other teams remain eligible to trade. Scope restrictions narrowly and monitor information barriers.
nodes.revisit: Surveillance shows leakage across a wall.

nodes.label: Who can override a warning?
nodes.context: Too strict and PMs lose trades; too loose and you lose your licence.
nodes.selected: PM overrides soft warnings with a reason
nodes.revisit: Override rates show rubber-stamping.
options: PM overrides soft warnings with a reason

nodes.label: PM overrides soft warnings with a reason
How is capital allocated across teams?
nodes.context: Verition’s stated approach reallocates capital as the opportunity set and risk/reward change. The proposed workflow makes team budgets, approvals and resulting limits explicit.
nodes.selected: CIO discretion informed by a model
nodes.revisit: The number of teams makes discretionary review impractical.
options: CIO discretion informed by a model

nodes.label: CIO discretion informed by a model
How are drawdowns handled?
nodes.context: Drawdown discipline is what protects the firm and its investors from any one team.
nodes.revisit: A strategy’s natural volatility makes the thresholds trigger on noise.
options: Hard stop at a single threshold

nodes.label: Hard stop at a single threshold
Which measure drives allocation?
nodes.context: Rewarding raw returns encourages risk-taking; rewarding Sharpe alone ignores diversification.
nodes.revisit: Teams cannot follow the measure; publish a simpler companion metric.

nodes.label: How are costs charged to teams?
nodes.context: Financing, market data, execution and technology costs are large and uneven across teams.
nodes.revisit: Shared-cost growth outpaces team P&L.
options: Full cost allocation with clear drivers

nodes.label: Full cost allocation with clear drivers
Which OMS vendor?
nodes.context: The OMS is expensive to replace once embedded.
nodes.revisit: Team count or asset classes outgrow the product.

nodes.label: Combined OEMS or separate OMS and EMS?
nodes.context: Execution needs differ widely by asset class.
nodes.revisit: Execution quality in an asset class lags.

nodes.label: How do OMS events reach the backbone?
nodes.context: Everything downstream depends on getting orders and fills out reliably.
nodes.revisit: The vendor has no event API; then drop copy plus API polling.

nodes.label: Broker algos, in-house algos, or an algo wheel?
nodes.context: Execution cost is a direct drag on team returns.
nodes.revisit: A team’s turnover makes in-house execution pay off.

nodes.label: How is TCA done?
nodes.context: Best execution must be evidenced, not asserted.
nodes.revisit: Never drop independent TCA.

nodes.label: Which FIX engine?
nodes.context: FIX sessions are business-critical during market hours.
nodes.revisit: Connection count makes per-session fees material.

nodes.label: How do you connect?
nodes.context: Latency, resilience and cost trade off directly.
nodes.revisit: A systematic team’s edge depends on microseconds.

nodes.label: Central hub or direct connections?
nodes.context: Several internal systems need external sessions.
nodes.revisit: Never at multi-manager scale.

nodes.label: Where does the IBOR live?
nodes.context: Every front-office number starts with positions.
nodes.revisit: You are early-stage; start on the platform IBOR and migrate later.

nodes.label: Which stream processor?
nodes.context: Positions must be exactly right and recover by replay.
nodes.revisit: State restore times exceed your recovery objective.

nodes.label: What is the position key?
nodes.context: Finer keys help recon; coarser keys perform better.
nodes.revisit: Never drop location in a multi-prime set-up.

nodes.label: Central matching or bilateral confirms?
nodes.context: US T+1 leaves hours, not days, to fix mismatches.
nodes.revisit: Never at scale.

nodes.label: Buy the platform or orchestrate in-house?
nodes.context: Post-trade is commodity but must be reliable.
nodes.revisit: Products the platform cannot handle become material.

nodes.label: How do you connect to SWIFT?
nodes.context: Settlement instructions and cash statements run on SWIFT.
nodes.revisit: Message volumes make bureau fees material.

nodes.label: Which message standard?
nodes.context: Cross-border payments moved to ISO 20022 in November 2025; securities still mostly use MT.
nodes.revisit: Custodians drop MT for securities settlement.

nodes.label: Spreadsheets or a treasury system?
nodes.context: Cash is where operational fraud happens.
nodes.revisit: Never.

nodes.label: Trust PB margin, or replicate it?
nodes.context: PB margin drives available leverage, so a team’s capacity.
nodes.revisit: Leverage is low enough that margin is not binding.

nodes.label: How is collateral chosen?
nodes.context: Delivering the wrong asset is expensive.
nodes.revisit: Funding cost becomes a visible drag.

nodes.label: Which accounting engine?
nodes.context: Administrators, auditors and investors all depend on these books.
nodes.revisit: You are choosing a full operations platform anyway.

nodes.label: Full shadow NAV, or rely on the admin?
nodes.context: The admin produces the official NAV; how much do you check?
nodes.revisit: Never at multi-manager scale.

nodes.label: Equalisation or series accounting?
nodes.context: Performance fees must be fair to investors who joined at different times.
nodes.revisit: The offering documents mandate equalisation.

nodes.label: Which reconciliation tool?
nodes.context: New counterparties and products appear constantly.
nodes.revisit: Volumes outgrow its pricing model.

nodes.label: How often do you reconcile?
nodes.context: A position break found next morning may already have caused a bad trade.
nodes.selected: Intraday for positions and cash at PBs
nodes.revisit: PBs cannot provide intraday data.
options: Intraday for positions and cash at PBs

nodes.label: Intraday for positions and cash at PBs
Who produces regulatory filings?
nodes.context: Form PF and Annex IV need risk data the admin does not have.
nodes.revisit: Filing scope is small enough to outsource.
options: Fully outsourced to admin or consultant

nodes.label: Fully outsourced to admin or consultant
Self-report transactions or delegate?
nodes.context: MiFIR and EMIR reporting is detailed and penalised for errors.
nodes.revisit: Delegated reporting quality fails QA.
options: Self-report via an approved reporting mechanism

nodes.label: Self-report via an approved reporting mechanism
Outsource transfer agency or run in-house?
nodes.context: TA is regulated, PII-heavy and not a source of edge.
nodes.revisit: Rarely.

nodes.label: How are side letters managed?
nodes.context: MFN clauses mean one investor’s terms can apply to others.
nodes.revisit: Never at scale.

nodes.label: Which authorisation model?
nodes.context: Teams must not see each other’s positions; ops must see everything but trade nothing.
nodes.revisit: Sharing becomes deeply hierarchical.

nodes.label: Okta or Entra?
nodes.context: The IdP is foundational.
nodes.revisit: Your SaaS estate leans heavily on Okta integrations.

nodes.label: Which API style internally?
nodes.context: Hundreds of service-to-service calls.
nodes.revisit: Partner integrations dominate.

nodes.label: How are counterparty files handled?
nodes.context: Most PB, custodian and admin data still arrives as files.
nodes.selected: Managed file transfer with expected-file calendar
nodes.revisit: Never.
options: Managed file transfer with expected-file calendar

nodes.label: Managed file transfer with expected-file calendar
Which observability backend?
nodes.context: Cost grows with data volume.
nodes.revisit: The bill exceeds a small platform team’s cost.

nodes.label: Build WORM storage or buy an archive?
nodes.context: Regulators fine firms heavily for record-keeping failures.
nodes.revisit: Never self-build communications archiving.

nodes.label: Cloud, colo or hybrid?
nodes.context: Most workloads are elastic; a few are latency-critical.
nodes.revisit: No team needs sub-millisecond execution.

nodes.label: Which DR strategy?
nodes.context: Trading must survive a region outage; back office can wait hours.
nodes.revisit: Trading RTO requirements tighten below minutes.

nodes.label: Central technology, embedded engineers, or both?
nodes.context: Investment teams want speed and tools specific to their strategy; the firm needs one platform, one set of controls and no duplicated systems.
nodes.selected: Platform teams plus small strategy squads
nodes.revisit: Squads repeatedly build things the platform should own, or platform queues slow teams down.
options: Engineers embedded in each investment team
Platform teams plus small strategy squads

nodes.label: Engineers embedded in each investment team
Platform teams plus small strategy squads
Organise teams by component, by business domain, or by asset class?
nodes.context: Team boundaries become system boundaries (Conway’s law). The architecture already has clear domains: trading, risk and capital, operations, finance, data.
nodes.selected: By business domain, owning whole components
nodes.revisit: A domain team grows beyond about 15–20 people; split it along a component boundary.
options: By business domain, owning whole components

nodes.label: By business domain, owning whole components

nodes.context: Data is produced in every domain, but the security master, governance and the analytical platform must be consistent firm-wide.
nodes.selected: Central platform and reference data; domains own their data products
nodes.revisit: Data quality issues trace back to unclear ownership between domains and the data office.
options: A central data team owns all data
Central platform and reference data; domains own their data products

Instruments & identifiers
nodes.description: Every tradable and referenced instrument with terms and every vendor identifier, across all asset classes.
nodes.recommendation: Shortlist Bloomberg Data License as the broad primary feed, with ICE as a specialist challenger for fixed income. Use OpenFIGI for identifier enrichment. Publish an internal instrument ID and field-level source hierarchy rather than adopting a vendor ID as the firm’s identity.
nodes.volume: Millions of instruments; tens of thousands of daily changes

nodes.label: Legal entities & issuers
nodes.description: Issuers, counterparties and their ownership hierarchy for limits, disclosures and counterparty exposure.
nodes.recommendation: Use GLEIF as the LEI baseline and shortlist Orbis for ownership and private-company enrichment. Use the primary reference vendor for issuer-to-instrument links. GLEIF parent relationships alone are not a complete beneficial-ownership or issuer-risk hierarchy.
nodes.selection_owner: CDO / Entity Data owner; CCO accepts disclosure hierarchy

nodes.label: Corporate actions
nodes.description: Dividends, splits, mergers, spin-offs, rights and elections with all key dates and terms.
nodes.recommendation: Reuse Bloomberg Reference Data as the primary announcement source if selected for instruments; compare ICE as a second source where coverage warrants it. Reconcile elections and entitlements to custodian/PB notices, which govern the actual account-level workflow.
nodes.selection_owner: Corporate Actions Operations; CDO owns ingestion

nodes.label: Funds, teams & books
nodes.description: The firm’s own structure: funds and share classes, strategy groups, investment teams, books, accounts at PBs and custodians.
nodes.recommendation: Keep funds, teams, books and account mappings in the internal capital/PMS master with approved changes. External platforms can host and distribute this structure; no market-data purchase can supply the firm’s authoritative organisation.
nodes.selection_owner: COO / CIO office; Finance approves fund and account structure

nodes.label: Ticks, quotes & bars
nodes.description: Trade and quote history at full granularity, plus derived bars for research and TCA.
nodes.recommendation: Shortlist LSEG Tick History for broad historical coverage and Databento for API-led research on its covered venues. Use direct exchange feeds where measured execution latency or full-depth needs justify the operational burden. Choose by strategy and venue rather than forcing one feed across all use cases.
nodes.selection_owner: Market Data product owner; Quant Research / Trading accept coverage
nodes.volume: Billions of rows per day; petabytes of history

nodes.label: EOD prices & official marks
nodes.description: Closing, evaluated and model prices with source, hierarchy level and overrides; the official set used for NAV.
nodes.recommendation: Use official exchange closes for eligible listed holdings; shortlist ICE for evaluated fixed-income marks and Bloomberg BVAL as an independent challenger. Set the source hierarchy by instrument and valuation policy, with documented challenge and override evidence.
nodes.volume: Millions of price points per day

nodes.label: Fundamentals & estimates
nodes.description: Company financials, KPIs and consensus estimates, point-in-time.
nodes.recommendation: Prefer a Compustat point-in-time package for standardised systematic fundamentals, with LSEG I/B/E/S for consensus estimates. Trial FactSet as an integrated alternative if existing research workflows make consolidation valuable. Confirm the specific historical-vintage product; a current financials feed is insufficient for unbiased backtesting.
nodes.selection_owner: Research Data lead / CDO; strategy heads approve usefulness
nodes.volume: Hundreds of millions of data points

nodes.label: Alternative data
nodes.description: Card spend, web, app, geolocation, satellite and sentiment datasets used for signals.
nodes.recommendation: Run hypothesis-led trials: YipitData for company/sector investor research, Similarweb for digital activity, and RavenPack for structured news/content signals. Buy only the categories that add reproducible incremental value after costs and existing-data overlap; there is no single preferred provider for all alternative data.
nodes.selection_owner: Research sponsor + CDO; CCO approves permitted use

nodes.label: Orders & executions
nodes.description: Every order, amendment, child order and fill, with full state history and raw FIX.
nodes.recommendation: Keep the chosen OMS as the order authority and retain independent broker/venue drop copies for fills. For a new selection, shortlist SS&C Eze for OMS workflow and FlexTRADER for specialist execution, subject to the broader sourcing decision. Buying a market-data feed cannot replace the firm’s order history.
nodes.selection_owner: Head of Trading; OMS/EMS product owners deliver

nodes.label: Transaction cost analysis
nodes.description: Benchmarks and costs per order: arrival, VWAP, implementation shortfall, broker and algo.
nodes.recommendation: Shortlist Virtu Analytics for a common multi-asset TCA baseline. Retain in-house signal-specific analysis for quant strategies, linked to the same orders and clocks. Assess confidentiality and conflicts associated with sharing orders with an execution-affiliated analytics provider.
nodes.selection_owner: Head of Trading / Best Execution Committee

nodes.label: Positions & tax lots
nodes.description: Positions by fund, book, instrument and location, intraday and EOD, with lot-level cost.
nodes.recommendation: Use the approved IBOR for the intraday investment view and accounting for official lot treatment; reconcile to PB/custodian statements. If buying an integrated book, shortlist Arcesium UBOR against the existing platform. Keep differences between trade-date, settlement-date and accounting positions explicit.
nodes.selection_owner: COO / IBOR owner; Finance owns accounting lots
nodes.volume: Hundreds of thousands of positions; millions of lots

nodes.label: Risk results
nodes.description: Exposures, sensitivities, VaR, stress and liquidity results from approved engines and independent providers. Photon is a candidate producer subject to coverage, reconciliation and contractual rights.
nodes.recommendation: Use the approved primary risk engine and an independent challenge process. Evaluate the reported Photon licence before committing to interfaces or model rights; public evidence here does not establish its exact product or scope. Shortlist Axioma for a separate risk-service evaluation where a material gap remains.
nodes.volume: Sizing assumption; profile with real workloads

nodes.label: Capital, performance & payouts
nodes.description: Capital allocated per team over time, performance analytics, drawdown events and payouts.
nodes.recommendation: Keep allocation decisions, mandates, rationale and payout rules in the internal capital service. Derive performance from approved position/pricing/accounting data and reconcile payouts to official books. No external dataset supplies the firm’s capital decisions or compensation policy.
nodes.selection_owner: CIO for capital; CFO for performance / payouts

nodes.label: Cash, settlement & payments
nodes.description: Settlement status, cash balances and movements, payments and FX.
nodes.recommendation: Source actual balances, payments and settlement status directly from contracted banks/custodians; compare them with internal projected cash. Shortlist Kyriba for multi-bank aggregation and treasury workflows only if the approved operations platform does not meet the need.
nodes.volume: Tens of thousands of messages per day

nodes.label: General ledger & NAV
nodes.description: Double-entry journals, NAV by share class, fees, accruals and performance.
nodes.recommendation: Retain the existing approved accounting platform if it supports the fund structure. For replacement, shortlist SS&C Geneva and Arcesium UBOR, then compare actual instrument/fee workflows. Obtain official NAV and sign-off evidence from the appointed administrator; platform output alone is not administrator approval.
nodes.volume: Millions of journal lines per month

nodes.label: Reconciliation & breaks
nodes.description: Recon runs, matched counts and every break with owner, age and root cause.
nodes.recommendation: Shortlist Duco for heterogeneous data reconciliation and exception workflows; retain SmartStream TLM where an existing implementation is effective. Export run, match and break history to the platform. A reconciliation tool produces control evidence from underlying sources; it does not supply independent positions or cash.
nodes.selection_owner: Head of Operations; CFO accepts material finance breaks

nodes.label: Investors & capital activity
nodes.description: Investor register, KYC status, subscriptions, redemptions and capital accounts.
nodes.recommendation: Use the appointed transfer agent’s register and dealing records as authoritative. Northern Trust Hedge Fund Services is a candidate if reviewing providers, but the public portal link does not confirm its contracted TA scope. Confirm the current appointment before recommending a change.
nodes.selection_owner: COO / Investor Services; CCO oversees KYC controls
nodes.volume: Profile after investor scope is confirmed
nodes.retention: Per AML rules (5+ years after relationship)

nodes.label: Compliance & surveillance
nodes.description: Restricted lists, wall-crossings, rule check results, breaches and surveillance alerts.
nodes.recommendation: Keep pre-trade decisions in the approved OMS/compliance engine and restrictions in the governed compliance master. Shortlist NICE Actimize for trade surveillance and Behavox for communications surveillance according to the control gap. They are distinct workflows and neither replaces synchronous pre-trade checks.

nodes.label: Regulatory reporting data
nodes.description: Governed mart producing Form PF, 13F, 13D/G, AIFMD Annex IV, CPO-PQR and regional disclosures.
nodes.recommendation: Build reconciled, reproducible reporting inputs in the internal mart and shortlist Confluence for the applicable filing regimes. Preserve signed-off filing snapshots and regulator acknowledgements. A filing tool supports submission; it does not validate the correctness of all source positions or legal classifications.
nodes.selection_owner: CCO / Regulatory Reporting; CFO owns financial inputs
